title: The Impact of Trade on Economic Prosperity

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Instrumental Variables (IV) approach using geographic distance as an instrument for trade volume. Geographic distance affects trade volume (relevance condition) but should not directly affect GDP per capita except through its effect on trade (exclusion restriction). The key assumptions are: (1) instrument relevance - distance is correlated with trade volume, (2) instrument exogeneity - distance only affects GDP per capita through trade volume, and (3) monotonicity - distance has a consistent directional effect on trade for all countries.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(AER)
library(stargazer)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s78_data.csv")

# Display basic summary statistics
cat("Summary Statistics:\n")
summary(data)

# First stage regression (instrument relevance check)
first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = data)
cat("\n=== FIRST STAGE REGRESSION ===\n")
cat("F-statistic for instrument relevance:", summary(first_stage)$fstatistic[1], "\n")
cat("Coefficient on distance (z):", coef(first_stage)["z"], "\n")
cat("P-value for distance:", summary(first_stage)$coefficients["z", "Pr(>|t|)"], "\n")

# OLS regression for comparison
ols_model <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = data)
cat("\n=== OLS RESULTS ===\n")
cat("OLS coefficient on trade volume:", coef(ols_model)["x"], "\n")

# Two-stage least squares (2SLS) estimation
iv_model <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = data)
cat("\n=== IV/2SLS RESULTS ===\n")
cat("IV coefficient on trade volume:", coef(iv_model)["x"], "\n")
cat("Standard error:", summary(iv_model)$coefficients["x", "Std. Error"], "\n")
cat("P-value:", summary(iv_model)$coefficients["x", "Pr(>|t|)"], "\n")

# Hausman test for endogeneity
hausman_test <- summary(iv_model, diagnostics = TRUE)
cat("\n=== DIAGNOSTIC TESTS ===\n")
cat("Wu-Hausman test p-value:", hausman_test$diagnostics["Wu-Hausman", "p-value"], "\n")
cat("Weak instruments test (Cragg-Donald):", hausman_test$diagnostics["Weak instruments", "statistic"], "\n")

# Reduced form regression
reduced_form <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = data)
cat("\n=== REDUCED FORM ===\n")
cat("Reduced form coefficient (distance on GDP):", coef(reduced_form)["z"], "\n")

# Calculate and display results table
cat("\n=== COMPARISON OF ESTIMATES ===\n")
cat(sprintf("OLS estimate: %.4f\n", coef(ols_model)["x"]))
cat(sprintf("IV estimate: %.4f\n", coef(iv_model)["x"]))
cat(sprintf("Difference: %.4f\n", coef(iv_model)["x"] - coef(ols_model)["x"]))

# Robustness check: Alternative specification without controls
iv_model_no_controls <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = data)
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECK (No Controls) ===\n")
cat("IV coefficient without controls:", coef(iv_model_no_controls)["x"], "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive coefficient on trade volume, indicating that increased international trade leads to higher GDP per capita, with a magnitude between 0.3-0.8. The IV estimate should be larger than the OLS estimate due to measurement error bias or reverse causality in OLS. Geographic distance should be negatively correlated with trade volume (first stage F-stat > 10), and the Hausman test should reject the null of exogeneity, justifying the IV approach. The effect represents the elasticity of GDP per capita with respect to trade volume.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use geographic distance as an instrument for trade volume to isolate its impact on GDP per capita.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Increased trade volume has a significant negative effect on log GDP per capita.
